# The Lights That Fall Without Warning

## Scripture
*"But about that day or hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father. Therefore keep watch, because you do not know on what day your Lord will come."* — Matthew 24:36, 42

## Reflection
Most nights, the sky keeps its appointments. Planets trace predictable paths. Constellations rise on schedule. You can set your watch by the heavens—until November, when the Leonids arrive.

Meteor showers are the sky's holy surprises. No calendar can promise exactly when a streak of light will cut across the dark. You can know the *season*, even the likely night—but the moment? That belongs to God alone. So watchers learn to simply lie back, eyes open, waiting.

Jesus told His followers to live the same way. Not frantic, not calculating—just awake. The Father holds the timing of all things, and our calling is not to predict but to be ready, watching with hopeful eyes.

There's something freeing in this. We don't have to decode the date. We don't have to master the schedule. We simply stay dressed for the journey, lamps trimmed, hearts turned skyward. And when the light falls—sudden, bright, unearned—we'll be looking up.

Tonight, step outside and watch for a while. Let the waiting itself become worship.

## Prayer
Father, we don't know the day or the hour, but we know You. Keep our hearts awake and our eyes lifted. Teach us to wait with joy, ready for the light whenever it falls. In Jesus' name, amen.
